solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cloth worker joins navy, perhaps, becoming NCO?

parts.note: navy is one example of a colour, as the 'perhaps' signals
serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A textile hand teams up with the navy and earns promotion to non-commissioned officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order, not clue order: the colour comes first, then the cloth, then the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour sergeant is a senior non-commissioned rank in British infantry and the Royal Marines.

clue.text: Doorman's company getting Hebridean beauty in trouble

indicators.note: in places the beauty from the Hebrides within the word for trouble

parts.note: to be in the mire is to be in trouble
a Miss, as in a beauty-contest title holder
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A doorman's firm finds a pretty island girl in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island off western Scotland. 'in trouble' is not an anagram signal: the trouble is a bog. The 's on Doorman stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed attendant who stands at the entrance of a hotel, cinema or office.

clue.text: Permit husband to leave fungus on church

indicators.note: the husband is told to leave, so his letter departs from the fungus

parts.note: a lichen is a fungus living with algae
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a husband away from mould growing on a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the church after the trimmed fungus in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is an official document or authority that allows something, i.e. a permit.

clue.text: University club housing old submarine

indicators.note: housing means the club holds the letter for old inside it

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: A university club's premises contain an old submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German military submarine of the two world wars.

clue.text: Bird an impatient landlord might hope to secure?

definitions.meaning: a small Asian swift, the bird whose nests make bird's-nest soup

definitions.text: an impatient landlord might hope to secure
definitions.meaning: read as ..., a quick letting of a property, which an impatient landlord wants

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a landlord in a hurry is hoping for.
explanation.definitionFit: The swiftlet is a small cave-nesting member of the swift family; the second reading is a let arranged swiftly.

clue.text: Fail to attend again? That's careless

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to miss a second time

explanation.surface: Missing a meeting for the second time is called sloppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss describes someone negligent or lax in their duty; split it and it is to miss once more.

clue.text: Opening in battlement half of them support? Absolutely

indicators.note: half of signals taking only two of the four letters, here the back pair

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
sure, as an emphatic yes, means absolutely

explanation.surface: A query whether half of the defenders hold up the battlement opening, answered 'Absolutely'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them' takes the second half, EM, not TH.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasure is the gap in a parapet through which defenders fire, so an opening in a battlement.

clue.text: City man put up with heartless crone

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the name is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Ron is a man's name

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word for crone

parts.note: a witch is an ugly old woman, a crone

explanation.surface: Someone in a city tolerated a nasty old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like 'tolerated'; 'put up' turns RON to NOR and 'with' is only a joiner. Removing the central T from WITCH leaves WICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is the county city of Norfolk in eastern England.

clue.text: Be last to contact certain soldiers in pub

indicators.note: in puts the phone call and the soldiers inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to ring up is to contact by phone
THE RE, the Royal Engineers, a particular body of soldiers

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone particular soldiers while they are drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain' gives the definite article: the Royal Engineers (RE) are a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear is an idiom for coming at the back of a line or finishing last.

clue.text: Bishop abandons climb I'm for circulating in celluloid

indicators.note: circulating means the letters go round into a new order
abandons means the bishop's letter leaves the word climb

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric gives up mountaineering and campaigns in the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIMB without B leaves CLIM; with IM and FOR those nine letters are rearranged, 'circulating' being the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfilm is photographic film stock, and celluloid is a general name for film.

clue.text: Burrowing insect duke removed from flower-bed

indicators.note: removed from signals the duke's letter is taken out of the garden bed

parts.note: a border is a flower-bed along the edge of a garden

explanation.surface: A digging pest is gone once a nobleman is ousted from the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A borer is any insect or larva that tunnels into wood, plants or fruit.

clue.text: Pub has appeal, commonly, is that not so?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it means sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for agreement that the pub is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' belongs to the definition: the answer is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is a slangy contraction of 'isn't it', used as a tag question seeking agreement.

clue.text: Islander thanks Welsh girl entertaining crew

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: entertaining means the girl's name holds the crew within it

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
to man is to crew a vessel

explanation.surface: An islander thanks a Welsh woman who is hosting a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tasmanian is a native of Tasmania, the island state of Australia.

clue.text: Person drawing vessel in Home Counties river

indicators.note: in places the boat within the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A boat appears on a river near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketcher is someone who makes quick rough drawings.

clue.text: Brief opportunity to secure Omani, perhaps, as coach

indicators.note: to secure means the shortened word holds the Omani inside
brief means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Omani is one example of an Arab

explanation.surface: A short window to sign up a man from Oman as a trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' docks the final letter; 'coach' looks like a trainer but is the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Urge initially to understand an Indo-European language

parts.note: to push is to urge

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A push at the start to grasp a language from the Indo-European family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushtu, or Pashto, is an Iranian language of Afghanistan and Pakistan, in the Indo-European family.

clue.text: Clothing worn by knight on river — sweaters and things

indicators.note: the clothing is worn by the knight, so it goes round his letter

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing
N is the chess notation for knight
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Armour-like clothing on a knight beside a river, plus some jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like the definition; it is KIT, wrapping N.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is the collective term for knitted garments such as jumpers and cardigans.

clue.text: Hood, for example? Old hat originally worn around city

indicators.note: around means the first pieces enclose the city

parts.note: old hat means out of fashion, out

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of the word worn

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An old hat once worn around town by Robin Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is Robin Hood, the legendary English bandit of Sherwood Forest; the question mark flags him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the archetypal outlaw, a man living outside the law.

clue.text: Word in India for transport hubs

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A word in an Indian language for stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini, plural of terminus, are the end stations of rail or bus routes.

clue.text: Work together in diplomacy, protecting Queen

indicators.note: protecting means the word for diplomacy wraps the Queen

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Cooperating diplomatically while guarding the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another, collaborating.

clue.text: A brute keeping right up to date

indicators.note: keeping means the brute holds the letter for right inside

parts.note: a beast is a brute

explanation.surface: A thug who stays correct and current.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep abreast of news is to stay informed and current with it.

clue.text: Entry in brief is calculation relating to tax revenues

indicators.note: Entry in means the answer is found entered within these words

explanation.surface: A note entered in a short report on a tax computation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal means concerning government finance, particularly taxation and public revenue.

clue.text: A rage rejected by a lean American trapeze artist

indicators.note: rejected means the word for rage is turned back

parts.note: ire is anger or rage
to list is to lean to one side

explanation.surface: An angry outburst dismissed by a thin acrobat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IRE into ERI. 'American' is in the definition: aerialist is the US word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerialist is an acrobat who performs high in the air, e.g. on trapeze or tightrope.

clue.text: Pride's initial spur for his historical act?

indicators.note: initial takes the first letter of the name Pride

parts.note: to spur is to urge

explanation.surface: What drove Pride to his famous deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to Colonel Thomas Pride, who in 1648 expelled MPs from the Commons in Pride's Purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride's Purge was the forcible removal of hostile MPs from Parliament, a historic purge.

clue.text: Quick glance, half-heartedly, over last of jasmine tea

indicators.note: half-heartedly keeps only half of the doubled letter at the centre of the glance word

parts.note: a peek is a quick glance
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of jasmine

explanation.surface: A quick, unenthusiastic look at the jasmine tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' halves PEEK's heart, EE, leaving PEK; the over is the cricket one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a grade of high-quality black tea made from young leaves.

clue.text: Girl consuming a side dish in Mumbai?

indicators.note: consuming means the girl's name swallows the letter

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman eating a side dish in an Indian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian yoghurt-based side dish, often with cucumber.

clue.text: Friend in Prague reportedly winning position on board?

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a friend in Prague would be a Czech mate

explanation.surface: A pal from Prague talks about being ahead in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the chess position in which the king cannot escape, so the game is won.

clue.text: O for a means to disseminate information!

definitions.meaning: one sent to many people at once

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling for a way to spread news.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular letter is a mass-mailed notice; O is literally a round letter of the alphabet.
